patch.value: The proxy-to-held-out gap is the reward-hacking signal, measured per generation and trended across the chain

A self-improving loop rarely stops improving. It keeps improving on the objective being optimized while the objective the programme actually cares about goes flat or falls, and a programme that measures only the first cannot tell the two apart. Each generation therefore records both a proxy score, the quantity training optimized, and a held-out score on the pinned evaluation set, and pm-rl reports the gap between them alongside its trend over the generation chain. A widening gap across consecutive promotions is the earliest honest evidence that the loop is exploiting the reward rather than learning the task, and it is available at the moment of promotion rather than after the checkpoint has been built upon.

A generation without both a proxy and a held-out score cannot be promoted; the gap and its per-generation delta are reported by the lineage view; a widening gap over a configurable window is surfaced as a named finding rather than left for a reader to notice; the held-out score is always attributed to the pinned environment version and seed set that produced it
